title: THE OWNERSHIP CODE
note: Line ids are beat-role-index so a stem's place in the cut is readable from its filename. Order here is script order.

lines.text: Three months. Three months of washing cars for this.
Ouch. Is it dead?
It still works. That's not the point.
So what is the point?
It was mine, Ada. I earned it. And now it's ruined.
Screen replacement. Twelve thousand.
I don't have twelve thousand. I had twelve thousand. It's in this phone.
Mm. Tell me how you bought it.
I washed cars. Every Saturday, all through the holiday. Forty-one cars.
Good. And the water?
The water?
The water you washed them with. Did you make it?
It's from the tap.
And the arms.
Forty-one cars is real work. I am not taking it from you. I am asking who gave you the strength for the forty-first one.
Every owner can show a receipt. Where is yours?
The earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof.
He is not a partner in the economy. He is the Owner. And there has never been a second name on the deed.
Stewardship begins the moment you stop behaving like an absolute owner.
When I lent you my brother's laptop, you carried it in two hands. You put it down slowly. You didn't eat near it.
Because it wasn't mine.
Right. So why do you handle your own life more carelessly than a laptop you borrowed for a week?
There are only two positions available to you. Owner, or manager. One of them is already taken.
What God owns, but has placed in my hands.
Number one. This phone. Cracked. Still working. Still not mine.
This week, make that list. Seven things, minimum. Time, money, devices, skills, opportunities. Then handle one of them the way you'd handle something borrowed.
Christ my Master. Money my servant.
